Corpay offers a variety of payment solutions that help to simplify, automate, secure, digitize and effectively control the way

businesses and consumers manage and pay their expenses. We provide our payment solutions to our business, merchant,

consumer and payment network customers in more than 200 countries a round the world today, although we operate primarily in

three geographies, with approximately 79% of our business in the U.S., Brazil and the U.K. Our customers may include

commercial businesses (obtained through direct and indirect channels) and partners for whom we manage payment programs,

We report information about our operating segments in accordance with the authoritative guidance related to segments. We

manage and report our operating results through the following three reportable segments: Corporate Payments, Vehicle

Payments and Lodging Payments. The remaining results are included within Other, which includes our Gift and Payroll Card

businesses. These segments align with how the Chief Operating Decision Maker (CODM) allocates resources, assesses

performance and reviews financial information.

Our revenue is generally reported net of the cost for underlying products and services purchased. In this report, we refer to this

oi.heading: Consolidated operating income
oi.text:
Consolidated operating income was $621.3 million in the three months ended September 30, 2026, an increase of 18.8% compared to the comparable prior period due to the reasons discussed above.

Other expense, net. Other expense, net was $10.2 million in the three months ended September 30, 2026, an increase of $8.8 million from the comparable prior period. This increase primarily represents net losses related to our equity method investments and the impact of fluctuations in foreign exchange rates on non-functional currency balances.

Interest expense, net. Interest expense, net was $108.8 million in the three months ended September 30, 2026, an increase of $8.7 million from the comparable prior period. The increase in interest expense was primarily due to increased borrowings used for acquisitions and share repurchases, partially offset by lower interest rates and higher interest income earned on higher cash balances. The following table sets forth the average interest rates paid on borrowings under our Credit Facility, excluding the related unused facility fees and swaps.

We have a portfolio of interest rate swaps, which are designated as cash flow hedges and cross-currency interest rate swaps, which are designated as net investment hedges.

opex.heading: Consolidated operating expenses
opex.text:
Processing. Processing expenses were $298.1 million in the three months ended September 30, 2026, an increase of 19.8% compared to the comparable prior period. Increases in processing expenses were primarily due to approximately $24 million of expenses related to acquisitions completed in 2025, higher variable expenses driven by increased transaction volumes, higher credit loss expense of approximately $21 million due to increased transaction volumes and higher fuel prices, investments to drive future growth and the unfavorable impact of foreign exchange rates of approximately $4 million. This increase was partially offset by lower expense of approximately $5 million from the impact of dispositions completed in 2025 and 2026.

Selling. Selling expenses were $145.4 million in the three months ended September 30, 2026, an increase of 23.6% from the comparable prior period. Increases in selling expenses were primarily due to marketing investments to drive future growth, increased commissions from higher sales volume, approximately $14 million of expenses related to acquisitions completed in 2025 and the unfavorable impact of foreign exchange rates of approximately $2 million. This increase was partially offset by lower expense of approximately $2 million from the impact of dispositions completed in 2025 and 2026.

General and administrative.

net sales.heading: Sources of Revenue
net sales.text:
Corpay offers a variety of payment solutions that simplify, automate, secure, digitize and effectively control the way businesses and consumers manage and pay their expenses. We provide our payment solutions to our business, merchant, consumer and payment network customers in more than 200 countries around the world today, although we operate primarily in three geograph ies, with approxima tely 76% of our busi ness in the U.S., Brazil and the U.K. Our customers may include commercial businesses (obtained through direct and indirect channels) and partners for whom we manage payment programs, as well as consumers.

We report information about our operating segments in accordance with the authoritative guidance related to segments. During the first quarter of 2026, the Company refined its segment composition within its existing reportable segments to reflect how our Chief Executive Officer, who is the Chief Operating Decision Maker (CODM), organizes and manages the global business. We manage and report our operating results through the following three reportable segments: Corporate Payments, Vehicle Payments and Lodging Payments. The remaining results are included within Other, which includes our Gift, Outsourced Card Processing and Payroll Card businesses.

lines.name: Cash and cash equivalents
lines.why: Cash can repay debt or be paid out: a financial asset. Cash needed to run the business is operating; move it if you know how much.

lines.name: Long-term investments
lines.why: Securities held for their return: financial. A stake in another business that is part of operations is operating.

lines.name: Receivables
lines.why: Owed by customers for sales: operating.

lines.name: Prepaid and other current assets
lines.why: Prepayments and other operating items: operating.

lines.name: Property, plant and equipment
lines.why: Assets used to produce and sell: operating.

lines.name: Operating lease right-of-use assets
lines.why: Leased stores, offices and equipment used in the business: operating.

lines.name: Goodwill
lines.why: Paid for acquired businesses: operating.

lines.name: Intangible assets
lines.why: Acquired technology, brands and customer relationships: operating.

lines.name: Equity-method investments
lines.why: Stakes in associated businesses, usually part of operations. Financial if held as an investment.

lines.name: Deferred tax assets
lines.why: Taxes on operating income paid ahead: operating.

lines.name: Other non-current assets
lines.why: Other long-term operating items: operating.

lines.name: Accounts payable
lines.why: Owed to suppliers for operations: operating.

lines.name: Accrued liabilities
lines.why: Services and other costs not yet paid: operating.

lines.name: Deferred revenue
lines.why: Customers' payments ahead of delivery: operating.

lines.name: Income taxes payable
lines.why: Taxes on operating income: operating.

lines.name: Other current liabilities
lines.why: Other operating items due within a year: operating.

lines.name: Current portion of long-term debt
lines.why: Borrowed money falling due within a year: financial.

lines.name: Long-term debt
lines.why: Bonds, notes and loans: financial.

lines.name: Operating lease liabilities
lines.why: Rent owed on leases used in the business: operating by default. Move it to financing to treat leases like debt (if the balance sheet has no lease line of its own, they sit inside other liabilities).

lines.name: Deferred tax liabilities
lines.why: Taxes on operating income deferred: operating.

lines.name: Other non-current liabilities
lines.why: Other long-term operating obligations: operating.

lines.name: Other current assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total current assets minus the current lines above: current assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other non-current assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Non-current assets (total assets − current assets) minus the non-current lines above: assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other current liabilities, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total current liabilities minus the current lines above: current liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other non-current liabilities, not tagged separately
lines.why: Non-current liabilities (total liabilities − current liabilities) minus the non-current lines above: liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

s.t: In conjunction with the closing of the AvidXchange transaction in October 2025, the Company invested approximately $ 578 million for approximately 35 % of the equity in the limited partnership with TPG for an enterprise valuation of approximately $ 1.9 billion.

In conjunction with the closing of the AvidXchange transaction in October 2025, we invested approximately $578 million for approximately 35% of the equity in the limited partnership for an enterprise valuation of approximately $1.9 billion.

• On October 31, 2025, we completed the acquisition of all of the ordinary shares of Alpha Group International plc ("Alpha"), a leading provider of B2B cross-border foreign exchange solutions to corporations and investment funds in the U.K. and Europe, for £42.50 in cash for each Alpha share, resulting in an aggregate purchase price of approximately £1.8 billion, or $2.4 billion.

In addition to other terms, the limited partnership agreement provides that, 33 months after the closing of the AvidXchange acquisition, the Company will have the right to acquire, or call, all the remaining outstanding equity of the limited partnership for approximately 2.5 times invested capital, which would result in the Company's consolidation of the limited partnership.
